Overview of the exposures investigated in the Puberty Cohort, The Danish National Birth Cohort, Denmark, 2000–21. For a detailed description of the exposures, please see the original articles.
Forrest plots of the associations between prenatal and childhood biological and psychosocial factors and puberty in boys (left) and girls (right), Puberty Cohort, DNBC, Denmark, 2000–21 [ 6 , 12–44 ]. Estimates (dots) are shown with 95% confidence intervals (horizontal lines) for each exposure group relative to the corresponding reference group indicated by the vertical black dotted line. Estimates and 95% confidence intervals are further shown to the right. (a) Genetic predisposition and congenital malformations; (b) maternal lifestyle factors in pregnancy; (c) demographic and psychosocial factors in pregnancy; (d) maternal dietary factors in pregnancy; (e) maternal diseases in pregnancy; (f) maternal use of medication in pregnancy; (g) maternal exposure to per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances in pregnancy; (h) birth-related and postpartum factors; (i) child health, anthropometrics, and psychosocial factors in childhood. Abbreviations: AAM, age at menarche; TTP, time to pregnancy; MAR, medically assisted reproduction; BMI, body mass index; PCOS, polycystic ovarian syndrome; INCS, intranasal corticosteroids; ICS, inhaled corticosteroids; PFOA, perfluorooctanoic acid; PFOS, perfluorooctane sulfonate; PFHxS, perfluorohexane sulfonic acid; PFHpS, perfluoroheptane sulfonic acid; PFNA, perfluorononanoic acid; PFDA, perfluorodecanoic acid.
Lollipop plots of the associations between prenatal and childhood biological and psychosocial factors and puberty listed according to the magnitude and direction of association in (a) boys and (b) girls, the Puberty Cohort, DNBC, Denmark, 2000–2021 [ 6 , 12–44 ]. The estimates are shown in dots and the magnitude of the associations are shown in vertical lines in color-coding according to the overall domain investigated. Abbreviations: BMI, body mass index; AAM, age at menarche; PCOS, polycystic ovarian syndrome; MAR, medically assisted reproduction; INCS, intranasal corticosteroids; ICS, inhaled corticosteroids.
